name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MULTI_STATEMENT_Q04 - Pancreatic endocrine regulation of blood glucose homeostasis

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements:

Statement I: The endocrine portion of the pancreas consists of Islets of Langerhans representing 1 to 2 percent of pancreatic tissue.

Statement II: Alpha cells of the Islets of Langerhans synthesize and secrete insulin, while beta cells secrete glucagon.

Statement III: Glucagon acts primarily on hepatocytes to stimulate glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, inducing hyperglycemia.

Statement IV: Insulin enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilization in hepatocytes and adipocytes, facilitating glycogenesis.

Statement V: Prolonged hyperglycemia and inadequate insulin secretion cause diabetes mellitus characterized by glycosuria and ketosis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: अग्न्याशय का अंतःस्रावी भाग लैंगरहैंस द्वीप समूह से बना होता है जो कुल अग्न्याशय ऊतक का केवल 1 से 2 प्रतिशत होता है।

कथन II: लैंगरहैंस द्वीप की अल्फा कोशिकाएं इंसुलिन का संश्लेषण व स्राव करती हैं, जबकि बीटा कोशिकाएं ग्लूकागॉन स्रावित करती हैं।

कथन III: ग्लूकागॉन मुख्य रूप से यकृत कोशिकाओं (हेपेटोसाइट्स) पर कार्य करके ग्लाइकोजिनोलिसिस और ग्लूकोनियोजेनेसिस को प्रेरित कर हाइपरग्लाइसीमिया करता है।

कथन IV: इंसुलिन हेपेटोसाइट्स और वसा ऊतक कोशिकाओं में ग्लूकोज के अंतर्ग्रहण और उपयोग को बढ़ाता है तथा ग्लाइकोजेनेसिस को सुगम बनाता है।

कथन V: दीर्घकालिक अतिरक्तशर्करा (हाइपरग्लाइसीमिया) और इंसुलिन की कमी से मधुमेह (डायबिटीज मेलिटस) रोग होता है जिसमें मूत्र में शर्करा और कीटोन काय बनते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Endocrine Pancreas Histological Proportions
The Islets of Langerhans constitute the endocrine pancreas, numbering roughly 1 to 2 million and making up about 1 to 2 percent of total pancreatic tissue. Hence, the first statement is factually correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pancreatic Islet Cell Secretions
Alpha cells secrete glucagon whereas beta cells synthesize and secrete insulin; the cellular secretory identities are reversed in the proposition. Hence, the second statement is factually incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Glucagon Hyperglycemic Actions
Glucagon promotes the breakdown of stored hepatic glycogen (glycogenolysis) and de novo synthesis of glucose (gluconeogenesis), elevating circulating blood sugar levels. Hence, the third statement is factually correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Insulin Hypoglycemic Actions
Insulin targets hepatocytes and adipocytes to enhance glucose uptake and stimulate glycogenic polymerization of glucose, reducing blood glucose concentration. Hence, the fourth statement is factually correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Diabetes Mellitus Pathophysiology
Chronic insulin deficiency and severe hyperglycemia lead to diabetes mellitus accompanied by urinary glucose excretion and ketone body formation. Hence, the fifth statement is factually correct.

Final Answer:
Only the first, third, fourth, and fifth statements are correct.

चरण 1: अग्न्याशय के अंतःस्रावी अनुपात का मूल्यांकन
लैंगरहैंस के द्वीप अग्न्याशय के अंतःस्रावी भाग का निर्माण करते हैं, जिनकी संख्या 10 से 20 लाख होती है और यह कुल ऊतक का 1-2% भाग बनाते हैं। अतः पहला कथन सही है।

चरण 2: द्वीपीय कोशिकाओं के स्राव का मूल्यांकन
अल्फा कोशिकाएं ग्लूकागॉन का स्राव करती हैं जबकि बीटा कोशिकाएं इंसुलिन का स्राव करती हैं; कथन में कोशिका प्रकार परस्पर उलट दिए गए हैं। अतः दूसरा कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: ग्लूकागॉन की हाइपरग्लाइसीमिक क्रिया का मूल्यांकन
ग्लूकागॉन यकृत में संचित ग्लाइकोजन के अपघटन और ग्लूकोज निर्माण को तेज कर रक्त शर्करा स्तर को बढ़ाता है। अतः तीसरा कथन सही है।

चरण 4: इंसुलिन की हाइपोग्लाइसीमिक क्रिया का मूल्यांकन
इंसुलिन यकृत और वसा कोशिकाओं द्वारा ग्लूकोज के अवशोषण को बढ़ाता है तथा ग्लाइकोजन संश्लेषण (ग्लाइकोजेनेसिस) को प्रेरित करता है। अतः चौथा कथन सही है।

चरण 5: डायबिटीज मेलिटस की विकृति का मूल्यांकन
दीर्घकालिक इंसुलिन की कमी से डायबिटीज मेलिटस रोग होता है, जिसमें मूत्र के साथ ग्लूकोज की हानि और हानिकारक कीटोन काय बनते हैं। अतः पाँचवाँ कथन सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर:
केवल पहला, तीसरा, चौथा और पाँचवाँ कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MULTI_STATEMENT_Q05 - Gonadal steroid hormones in male and female physiology

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements:

Statement I: Leydig cells located in the intertubular spaces of the testis synthesize androgens, primarily testosterone.

Statement II: Androgens stimulate protein catabolism and muscle wasting while suppressing male spermatogenesis.

Statement III: Estrogen is synthesized and secreted primarily by the growing ovarian follicles in the female ovary.

Statement IV: Following ovulation, the ruptured follicle transforms into the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone.

Statement V: Progesterone supports pregnancy and promotes alveolar development and secretory activity in mammary glands.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: वृषण के अंतराली स्थानों में उपस्थित लेडिग कोशिकाएं एंड्रोजेन्स, मुख्य रूप से टेस्टोस्टेरोन का संश्लेषण करती हैं।

कथन II: एंड्रोजेन्स प्रोटीन के अपचय और पेशियों के क्षय को प्रेरित करते हैं तथा नर में शुक्राणुजनन को दबाते हैं।

कथन III: मादा अंडाशय में मुख्य रूप से वृद्धि करते हुए डिम्बग्रंथि पुटक एस्ट्रोजन का संश्लेषण और स्राव करते हैं।

कथन IV: अंडोत्सर्ग के पश्चात, फटा हुआ पुटक कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम में परिवर्तित हो जाता है, जो प्रोजेस्टेरोन स्रावित करता है।

कथन V: प्रोजेस्टेरोन सगर्भता को सहारा देता है तथा स्तन ग्रंथियों में कूपिकाओं (एल्विओलाई) के विकास और दुग्ध स्राव को प्रेरित करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Testicular Leydig Cell Endocrine Function
The interstitial Leydig cells positioned between seminiferous tubules synthesize and secrete male steroid hormones termed androgens, predominantly testosterone. Hence, the first statement is factually correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Androgen Metabolic and Spermatogenic Actions
Androgens exert anabolic (synthetic) effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism, stimulate muscular hypertrophy, and promote spermatogenesis; they do not cause catabolic wasting or suppress gametogenesis. Hence, the second statement is factually incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Ovarian Estrogen Synthesis
Growing ovarian follicles under gonadotrophic stimulation actively synthesize and release estrogen, driving female secondary sexual characteristics. Hence, the third statement is factually correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Corpus Luteum Formation and Endocrine Function
Following ovulation, granulosa and theca remnants of the ruptured Graafian follicle luteinize into the corpus luteum to secrete large amounts of progesterone. Hence, the fourth statement is factually correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Progesterone Gestational Actions
Progesterone maintains the uterine endometrium during gestation, supports pregnancy, and stimulates alveolar development in mammary glands. Hence, the fifth statement is factually correct.

Final Answer:
Only the first, third, fourth, and fifth statements are correct.

चरण 1: वृषण की लेडिग कोशिकाओं के कार्य का मूल्यांकन
शुक्रजनक नलिकाओं के बीच स्थित अंतराली लेडिग कोशिकाएं टेस्टोस्टेरोन सहित एंड्रोजेन्स का संश्लेषण करती हैं। अतः पहला कथन सही है।

चरण 2: एंड्रोजन के उपापचयी व शुक्राणुजनक प्रभाव का मूल्यांकन
एंड्रोजन प्रोटीन पर उपचयी (एनाबॉलिक) प्रभाव डालते हैं, पेशीय वृद्धि बढ़ाते हैं और शुक्राणुजनन को प्रेरित करते हैं; ये अपचय या दमन नहीं करते। अतः दूसरा कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: अंडाशयी एस्ट्रोजन संश्लेषण का मूल्यांकन
वृद्धि करते हुए डिम्बग्रंथि पुटक मुख्य रूप से एस्ट्रोजन का संश्लेषण करते हैं, जो द्वितीयक लैंगिक लक्षणों को प्रेरित करता है। अतः तीसरा कथन सही है।

चरण 4: कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम के निर्माण और कार्य का मूल्यांकन
अंडोत्सर्ग के बाद टूटा हुआ ग्राफी पुटक कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम बन जाता है जो भारी मात्रा में प्रोजेस्टेरोन स्रावित करता है। अतः चौथा कथन सही है।

चरण 5: प्रोजेस्टेरोन की सगर्भता में भूमिका का मूल्यांकन
प्रोजेस्टेरोन सगर्भता (गर्भावस्था) को बनाए रखता है और स्तन ग्रंथियों में कूपिकाओं (एल्विओलाई) के निर्माण को प्रेरित करता है। अतः पाँचवाँ कथन सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर:
केवल पहला, तीसरा, चौथा और पाँचवाँ कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MULTI_STATEMENT_Q06 - Non-endocrine organ hormones and cellular receptor mechanisms

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements:

Statement I: The atrial myocardium of the heart produces atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), which induces vasodilation and lowers blood pressure.

Statement II: Juxtaglomerular cells in the kidney produce erythropoietin, which stimulates the production of erythrocytes.

Statement III: Cholecystokinin (CCK) acts on both the pancreas and gall bladder to stimulate pancreatic enzyme and bile secretion.

Statement IV: Water-soluble peptide hormones freely cross the lipid bilayer to bind directly to nuclear chromatin receptors.

Statement V: Lipid-soluble steroid hormones and iodothyronines bind to intracellular receptors to modulate gene expression and transcription.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: हृदय की आलिंद भित्ति एट्रियल नैट्रियूरेटिक कारक (ANF) उत्पन्न करती है, जो वाहिकाविस्फारण कर रक्तदाब को कम करता है।

कथन II: वृक्क की जक्स्टाग्लोमेरुलर कोशिकाएं एरिथ्रोपोइटिन बनाती हैं, जो लाल रक्त कणिकाओं (एरिथ्रोपोइसेस) के निर्माण को प्रेरित करता है।

कथन III: कोलीसिस्टोकाइनिन (CCK) अग्न्याशय और पित्ताशय दोनों पर कार्य कर पाचक एंजाइम तथा पित्त रस के स्राव को प्रेरित करता है।

कथन IV: जल-विलेय पेप्टाइड हॉर्मोन लिपिड द्विपरत को स्वतंत्र रूप से पार कर सीधे केंद्रक के क्रोमैटिन ग्राही से जुड़ते हैं।

कथन V: वसा-विलेय स्टेरॉयड हॉर्मोन और आयोडोथाइरोनीन अंतःकोशिकीय ग्राहियों से जुड़कर जीन अभिव्यक्ति और अनुलेखन को नियंत्रित करते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Atrial Natriuretic Factor Secretion
When blood pressure rises, atrial cardiomyocytes secrete atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), which induces systemic vasodilation to reduce blood pressure. Hence, the first statement is factually correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Renal Erythropoietin Secretion
Juxtaglomerular cells in renal tissue synthesize the peptide hormone erythropoietin, which stimulates bone marrow erythropoiesis. Hence, the second statement is factually correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Cholecystokinin Physiological Targets
Cholecystokinin (CCK) coordinates digestive secretions by stimulating exocrine pancreatic acinar enzyme secretion and triggering gall bladder contraction for bile discharge. Hence, the third statement is factually correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Peptide Hormone Membrane-Bound Mechanism
Peptide hormones are hydrophilic and cannot penetrate the hydrophobic core of the plasma membrane; they bind cell-surface receptors and generate second messengers rather than diffusing to chromatin. Hence, the fourth statement is factually incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of Intracellular Steroid Signaling Mechanism
Lipophilic steroid hormones and iodothyronines cross plasma membranes and attach to intracellular receptors, forming hormone-receptor complexes that interact with genomic DNA to regulate transcription. Hence, the fifth statement is factually correct.

Final Answer:
Only the first, second, third, and fifth statements are correct.

चरण 1: एट्रियल नैट्रियूरेटिक कारक के स्राव का मूल्यांकन
रक्तदाब बढ़ने पर हृदय की आलिंद भित्ति ANF स्रावित करती है, जो रक्त वाहिकाओं का विस्फारण कर रक्तचाप को घटाता है। अतः पहला कथन सही है।

चरण 2: वृक्क के एरिथ्रोपोइटिन स्राव का मूल्यांकन
वृक्क की जक्स्टाग्लोमेरुलर कोशिकाएं एरिथ्रोपोइटिन नामक पेप्टाइड हॉर्मोन बनाती हैं जो रक्ताणु निर्माण (एरिथ्रोपोइसेस) को प्रेरित करता है। अतः दूसरा कथन सही है।

चरण 3: कोलीसिस्टोकाइनिन के शारीरिक लक्ष्यों का मूल्यांकन
CCK अग्न्याशय पर कार्य करके अग्न्याशयी एंजाइमों के स्राव को और पित्ताशय पर कार्य करके पित्त रस के निष्कासन को प्रेरित करता है। अतः तीसरा कथन सही है।

चरण 4: पेप्टाइड हॉर्मोन की झिल्ली-बद्ध कार्यप्रणाली का मूल्यांकन
जल-विलेय पेप्टाइड हॉर्मोन कोशिका झिल्ली को पार नहीं कर सकते; वे कोशिका सतह के ग्राहियों से जुड़कर द्वितीयक संदेशवाहक बनाते हैं, न कि क्रोमैटिन से सीधे जुड़ते हैं। अतः चौथा कथन गलत है।

चरण 5: स्टेरॉयड हॉर्मोन की अंतःकोशिकीय क्रिया का मूल्यांकन
लिपिड-विलेय स्टेरॉयड हॉर्मोन और थाइरॉइड हॉर्मोन झिल्ली को पार कर अंतःकोशिकीय ग्राहियों से जुड़ते हैं और जीनोम के साथ परस्पर क्रिया कर जीन अभिव्यक्ति को नियंत्रित करते हैं। अतः पाँचवाँ कथन सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर:
केवल पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और पाँचवाँ कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q01 - Matching endocrine glands with their primary secretions

questiontext.text:
Match the endocrine glands in List I with their primary hormone secretions in List II:

List I (Endocrine Gland) List II (Hormone Secretion)
A. Pineal glandI. Parathyroid hormone
B. Thyroid glandII. Melatonin
C. Parathyroid glandIII. Thymosins
D. Thymus glandIV. Tetraiodothyronine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Organised endocrine glands in the human body possess specialized secretory tissues that synthesize distinct regulatory hormones responsible for maintaining physiological homeostasis.

Step 2: Biochemical and Endocrine Correlations
- The pineal gland, situated on the dorsal side of the forebrain, secretes melatonin to regulate 24-hour diurnal body rhythms.
- The follicular cells of the thyroid gland synthesize tetraiodothyronine (thyroxine or T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) to regulate basal metabolic rate.
- The parathyroid glands, located on the posterior surface of the thyroid lobes, produce parathyroid hormone (PTH) to elevate circulating calcium levels.
- The thymus gland, located behind the sternum on the ventral side of the aorta, secretes peptide hormones named thymosins to promote T-lymphocyte differentiation.

Step 3: Synthesis and Evaluation
Correlating each endocrine organ with its specific secretory product confirms that the pineal gland aligns with melatonin, the thyroid gland aligns with tetraiodothyronine, the parathyroid gland aligns with parathyroid hormone, and the thymus gland aligns with thymosins.

Final Answer:
The correct matching pairs pineal gland with melatonin, thyroid gland with tetraiodothyronine, parathyroid gland with parathyroid hormone, and thymus gland with thymosins.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q02 - Matching anterior pituitary hormones with target actions

questiontext.text:
Match the pituitary hormones in List I with their primary target physiological actions in List II:

List I (Pituitary Hormone) List II (Target Action)
A. ProlactinI. Stimulates synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids
B. Adrenocorticotropic hormoneII. Induces ovulation and maintains corpus luteum
C. Luteinizing hormoneIII. Stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes in renal distal tubules
D. VasopressinIV. Regulates growth of mammary glands and milk formation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The pituitary gland secretes trophic and regulatory peptides that act on peripheral endocrine targets and effector tissues to coordinate somatic development, reproduction, and fluid conservation.

Step 2: Functional Hormone Pairing
- Prolactin regulates mammary gland development and stimulates the synthesis and formation of milk within alveolar tissue.
- Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) targets the adrenal cortex to stimulate the synthesis and secretion of steroid glucocorticoids.
- Luteinizing hormone (LH) in females induces ovulation of mature graafian follicles and maintains the secretory activity of the corpus luteum.
- Vasopressin (anti-diuretic hormone) targets the distal renal tubules and collecting ducts of the kidney to stimulate water and electrolyte reabsorption, preventing excessive urinary loss.

Step 3: Verification of Endocrine Roles
Checking each hormone against its primary physiological target confirms that prolactin pairs with mammary gland milk formation, ACTH pairs with glucocorticoid secretion, LH pairs with ovulation and corpus luteum maintenance, and vasopressin pairs with distal tubular water resorption.

Final Answer:
The correct matching pairs prolactin with mammary gland milk formation, adrenocorticotropic hormone with glucocorticoid secretion, luteinizing hormone with ovulation, and vasopressin with renal water resorption.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q03 - Matching endocrine disorders with diagnostic clinical manifestations

questiontext.text:
Match the endocrine disorders in List I with their characteristic clinical features in List II:

List I (Endocrine Disorder) List II (Characteristic Feature)
A. AcromegalyI. Stunted growth, low intelligence quotient, and deaf-mutism in infants
B. CretinismII. Acute weakness, severe fatigue, and altered carbohydrate metabolism
C. Graves' diseaseIII. Severe facial disfigurement due to growth hormone hypersecretion in adults
D. Addison's diseaseIV. Exophthalmic goitre with protruding eyeballs and elevated metabolic rate

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Endocrine pathologies arise from either hyposecretion or hypersecretion of specific hormones, each leading to recognizable clinical symptoms and anatomical changes.

Step 2: Pathophysiological Correlations
- Acromegaly is caused by excess secretion of growth hormone during adulthood (particularly middle age), leading to severe disfigurement of facial bones and extremities.
- Cretinism occurs due to maternal hypothyroidism during pregnancy, which impairs fetal development and results in stunted physical growth, mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin, and deaf-mutism.
- Graves' disease (exophthalmic goitre) is an autoimmune form of hyperthyroidism characterised by an enlarged thyroid gland, prominent protrusion of the eyeballs, weight loss, and an elevated basal metabolic rate.
- Addison's disease results from underproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex, which disrupts carbohydrate and mineral metabolism and produces extreme asthenia, fatigue, and weakness.

Step 3: Synthesis of Clinical Associations
Evaluating these pathological conditions confirms that acromegaly corresponds to adult facial disfigurement, cretinism corresponds to neonatal developmental and intellectual deficits, Graves' disease corresponds to exophthalmic goitre, and Addison's disease corresponds to adrenal cortical insufficiency with acute weakness.

Final Answer:
The correct matching pairs acromegaly with adult facial disfigurement, cretinism with congenital developmental defects, Graves' disease with exophthalmic goitre and elevated BMR, and Addison's disease with acute weakness from adrenal cortical insufficiency.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q04 - Matching corticoid and thyroid hormones with physiological functions

questiontext.text:
Match the hormones in List I with their primary metabolic and physiological functions in List II:

List I (Hormone) List II (Physiological Function)
A. AldosteroneI. Stimulates gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, and produces anti-inflammatory reactions
B. CortisolII. Lowers blood calcium levels by regulating calcium homeostasis
C. ThyrocalcitoninIII. Stimulates breakdown of glycogen, increasing alertness and pupillary dilation
D. EpinephrineIV. Stimulates reabsorption of sodium and water and excretion of potassium

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Adrenal and thyroid hormones regulate electrolyte balance, organic energy metabolism, calcium concentrations, and emergency sympathetic responses in vertebrates.

Step 2: Functional Differentiation of Hormones
- Aldosterone (the principal mineralocorticoid) acts on the distal convoluted tubules to stimulate the reabsorption of sodium ions and water while enhancing potassium and phosphate excretion, maintaining osmotic pressure and blood pressure.
- Cortisol (the primary glucocorticoid) stimulates gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, and proteolysis, inhibits cellular amino acid uptake, suppresses inflammatory responses, and promotes RBC formation.
- Thyrocalcitonin (TCT), a thyroid peptide hormone, regulates blood calcium levels by reducing hypercalcemia and maintaining bone mineral integrity.
- Epinephrine (adrenaline), a catecholamine from the adrenal medulla, triggers the fight-or-flight response by accelerating glycogenolysis, raising blood glucose, dilating pupils, and increasing cardiac contractility.

Step 3: Verification of Physiological Pairs
Aligning each hormone confirms that aldosterone pairs with renal sodium and water reabsorption, cortisol pairs with gluconeogenesis and anti-inflammatory activity, thyrocalcitonin pairs with blood calcium reduction, and epinephrine pairs with fight-or-flight glycogenolysis and pupillary dilation.

Final Answer:
The correct matching pairs aldosterone with renal sodium reabsorption, cortisol with gluconeogenesis and anti-inflammatory reactions, thyrocalcitonin with blood calcium regulation, and epinephrine with sympathetic glycogen breakdown and pupillary dilation.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q05 - Matching digestive and renal hormones with physiological targets

questiontext.text:
Match the gastrointestinal and renal peptide hormones in List I with their target organs and actions in List II:

List I (Hormone) List II (Target Organ and Action)
A. GastrinI. Exocrine pancreas to stimulate secretion of water and bicarbonate ions
B. SecretinII. Bone marrow to stimulate erythropoiesis (red blood cell formation)
C. CholecystokininIII. Gastric glands to stimulate hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen secretion
D. ErythropoietinIV. Gall bladder and pancreas to stimulate bile and digestive enzyme secretion

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Enteric endocrine cells and renal juxtaglomerular cells produce specialized peptide regulatory hormones that control exocrine digestive secretions and stimulate red blood cell production.

Step 2: Functional Target Analysis
- Gastrin is secreted by mucosal cells of the stomach and acts directly on gastric glands to stimulate the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) and pepsinogen.
- Secretin is released from the duodenum in response to acid chyme and acts on the exocrine pancreas to stimulate abundant water and bicarbonate ion secretion.
- Cholecystokinin (CCK) stimulates both the gall bladder to contract and release bile and the exocrine pancreas to release pancreatic digestive enzymes.
- Erythropoietin is synthesized by the juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney and targets hematopoietic stem tissue to stimulate the production of red blood cells (erythropoiesis).

Step 3: Verification of Endocrine Assignments
Assessing all four hormones shows that gastrin corresponds to gastric acid and pepsinogen secretion, secretin corresponds to pancreatic water and bicarbonate secretion, CCK corresponds to bile and pancreatic enzyme release, and erythropoietin corresponds to erythropoiesis stimulation.

Final Answer:
The correct matching pairs gastrin with gastric acid secretion, secretin with pancreatic bicarbonate release, cholecystokinin with gall bladder and pancreatic enzyme release, and erythropoietin with erythropoiesis stimulation.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q06 - Matching glycemic and calcium regulatory hormones with actions

questiontext.text:
Match the homeostatic regulatory hormones in List I with their metabolic actions in List II:

List I (Hormone) List II (Metabolic Action)
A. InsulinI. Stimulates osteoclastic bone demineralisation and raises blood calcium
B. GlucagonII. Causes vasodilation of blood vessels to lower systemic blood pressure
C. Parathyroid hormoneIII. Stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, producing hyperglycemia
D. Atrial natriuretic factorIV. Enhances cellular glucose uptake and glycogenesis, producing hypoglycemia

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Homeostatic balance of blood glucose, serum calcium, and arterial pressure is regulated by counter-regulatory hormones operating through negative feedback mechanisms.

Step 2: Analysis of Endocrine Functions
- Insulin acts predominantly on hepatocytes and adipocytes, facilitating cellular uptake of glucose from the blood and stimulating glycogenesis, thereby lowering blood glucose levels as a hypoglycemic factor.
- Glucagon acts on liver hepatocytes to stimulate glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, raising blood glucose concentration as a hyperglycemic factor.
- Parathyroid hormone (PTH) stimulates bone resorption (demineralisation) and promotes renal and enteric calcium uptake, elevating blood calcium as a hypercalcemic factor.
- Atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), released by the cardiac atrial walls in response to hypertension, triggers systemic vasodilation to lower arterial blood pressure.

Step 3: Verification of Hormone Correlations
Comparing these physiological roles confirms that insulin aligns with enhanced glucose uptake and glycogenesis, glucagon aligns with glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, parathyroid hormone aligns with bone demineralisation and hypercalcemia, and ANF aligns with vasodilation and blood pressure reduction.

Final Answer:
The correct matching pairs insulin with glucose uptake and glycogenesis, glucagon with glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, parathyroid hormone with bone demineralisation, and atrial natriuretic factor with vasodilation and blood pressure reduction.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q07 - Matching reproductive and circadian hormones with biological roles

questiontext.text:
Match the reproductive and regulatory hormones in List I with their primary biological roles in List II:

List I (Hormone) List II (Biological Role)
A. TestosteroneI. Regulates 24-hour diurnal sleep-wake cycle and body temperature
B. EstrogenII. Supports pregnancy and stimulates development of mammary alveoli
C. ProgesteroneIII. Stimulates spermatogenesis, muscular growth, and male secondary characters
D. MelatoninIV. Stimulates growth and activities of female secondary sex organs and follicles

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sex steroids from male and female gonads govern gametogenesis, accessory sex organ development, and secondary sexual characteristics, while pineal secretions govern circadian rhythmicity.

Step 2: Functional Associations
- Testosterone (the primary androgen from Leydig cells) stimulates spermatogenesis, somatic muscle growth, male secondary sex characters, aggressiveness, and libido.
- Estrogen (secreted by developing ovarian follicles) stimulates the growth and functional activities of female secondary sex organs, ovarian follicles, and feminine secondary sex traits.
- Progesterone (secreted by the corpus luteum) is essential for maintaining the uterine lining during pregnancy and stimulates the formation of milk-storing alveoli in mammary glands.
- Melatonin (produced by the pineal gland) coordinates diurnal biorhythms, including the 24-hour sleep-wake cycle and core body temperature fluctuation.

Step 3: Verification of Alignments
Reviewing the four hormones confirms that testosterone corresponds to spermatogenesis and male secondary traits, estrogen corresponds to female secondary sex organ development, progesterone corresponds to pregnancy support and alveolar development, and melatonin corresponds to 24-hour diurnal sleep-wake regulation.

Final Answer:
The correct matching pairs testosterone with spermatogenesis and male traits, estrogen with female secondary sex organ growth, progesterone with pregnancy support, and melatonin with 24-hour diurnal sleep-wake rhythm regulation.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q08 - Matching representative human hormones with chemical classes

questiontext.text:
Match the representative human hormones in List I with their chemical classification in List II:

List I (Hormone) List II (Chemical Classification)
A. CortisolI. Iodothyronine
B. EpinephrineII. Peptide and protein hormone
C. GlucagonIII. Steroid hormone
D. ThyroxineIV. Amino-acid derivative

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hormones are categorized biochemically based on their chemical structure into peptides/proteins, steroids, iodothyronines, and amino-acid derivatives, which fundamentally influences their solubility and mechanism of action.

Step 2: Biochemical Classification Analysis
- Cortisol is a glucocorticoid synthesized from cholesterol within the adrenal cortex, classifying it definitively as a steroid hormone.
- Epinephrine is a catecholamine synthesized via modification of the amino acid tyrosine, classifying it as an amino-acid derivative.
- Glucagon is a 29-amino acid single-chain polypeptide synthesized by pancreatic alpha cells, classifying it as a peptide, polypeptide, or protein hormone.
- Thyroxine (tetraiodothyronine or T4) is an iodinated derivative of thyronine synthesized in thyroid follicles, classifying it as an iodothyronine.

Step 3: Verification of Classification Pairs
Evaluating each hormone confirms that cortisol aligns with steroid hormone, epinephrine aligns with amino-acid derivative, glucagon aligns with peptide/protein hormone, and thyroxine aligns with iodothyronine.

Final Answer:
The correct matching pairs cortisol with steroid hormone, epinephrine with amino-acid derivative, glucagon with peptide and protein hormone, and thyroxine with iodothyronine.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q09 - Matching hormone classes with receptor mechanisms and responses

questiontext.text:
Match the hormones in List I with their receptor interaction and signal transduction pathways in List II:

List I (Hormone) List II (Receptor and Signaling Pathway)
A. Follicle stimulating hormoneI. Binds intracellular nuclear receptors to regulate gene expression directly
B. EstrogenII. Reversible membrane interaction generating cyclic AMP as second messenger
C. SomatostatinIII. Hypothalamic axonal release into hypophyseal portal circulation
D. OxytocinIV. Axonally transported from hypothalamus and stored in neurohypophysis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hormonal communication operates through distinct physical mechanisms: peptide hormones interact with membrane-bound receptors to trigger second messengers, lipid-soluble hormones enter cells to bind nuclear receptors, and hypothalamic neurohormones follow distinct portal or neural distribution routes.

Step 2: Signal Transduction and Delivery Mechanisms
- Follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) is a large glycoprotein that binds to transmembrane membrane-bound receptors on ovarian target cells, activating adenylate cyclase to generate cyclic AMP and calcium as second messengers.
- Estrogen is a lipophilic steroid that diffuses across the target cell membrane and binds to intracellular nuclear receptors, where the hormone-receptor complex interacts directly with the genome to regulate gene transcription.
- Somatostatin is a regulatory hypothalamic peptide released at nerve terminals into the hypophyseal portal system to inhibit anterior pituitary growth hormone secretion.
- Oxytocin is synthesized by hypothalamic neurosecretory nuclei, transported along axons down the pituitary stalk, and stored for release in the neurohypophysis.

Step 3: Verification of Pathway Allocations
Assessing the mechanisms demonstrates that FSH corresponds to membrane receptor signaling with cyclic AMP generation, estrogen corresponds to intracellular nuclear genomic regulation, somatostatin corresponds to portal transport to the adenohypophysis, and oxytocin corresponds to axonal transport and neurohypophysial storage.

Final Answer:
The correct matching pairs follicle stimulating hormone with membrane receptor second-messenger signaling, estrogen with intracellular nuclear receptor gene regulation, somatostatin with hypothalamic portal secretion, and oxytocin with axonal transport to the neurohypophysis.

answer.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q10 - Matching endocrine tissue zones with secretions and functions

questiontext.text:
Match the histological zones and endocrine regions in List I with their primary hormone products and functions in List II:

List I (Histological Region) List II (Hormone Product and Function)
A. Zona glomerulosaI. Glucocorticoids (cortisol) regulating carbohydrate, fat, and protein catabolism
B. Zona fasciculataII. Catecholamines regulating emergency fight-or-flight cardiovascular responses
C. Adrenal medullaIII. Mineralocorticoids (aldosterone) regulating electrolyte and water balance
D. Corpus luteumIV. Progesterone supporting pregnancy and maintaining the uterine endometrium

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Endocrine glands are compartmentalized into distinct anatomical and histological zones, each specialized to synthesize distinct classes of regulatory hormones.

Step 2: Histological and Secretory Differentiation
- Zona glomerulosa (the outermost cortex layer of the adrenal gland) secretes mineralocorticoids, primarily aldosterone, which govern renal tubular reabsorption of electrolytes and fluid balance.
- Zona fasciculata (the intermediate and thickest cortical zone) secretes glucocorticoids, primarily cortisol, which control gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, proteolysis, and anti-inflammatory activity.
- The adrenal medulla (central neuroendocrine tissue) contains chromaffin cells that secrete catecholamines (adrenaline and noradrenaline) to mediate rapid emergency cardiovascular and metabolic adjustments.
- The corpus luteum (formed from post-ovulatory ovarian follicular tissue) produces high concentrations of progesterone, which maintains the uterine endometrium and supports gestational development.

Step 3: Verification of Zonal Secretions
Evaluating each histological compartment verifies that zona glomerulosa aligns with mineralocorticoids (aldosterone), zona fasciculata aligns with glucocorticoids (cortisol), adrenal medulla aligns with catecholamines, and corpus luteum aligns with gestational progesterone.

Final Answer:
The correct matching pairs zona glomerulosa with mineralocorticoids regulating electrolyte balance, zona fasciculata with glucocorticoids regulating carbohydrate metabolism, adrenal medulla with emergency catecholamines, and corpus luteum with gestational progesterone.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q01 - Sequence of signal transduction for peptide hormones

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following sequential events occurring during the mechanism of action of a protein hormone (e.g., FSH) on its target cell in the correct chronological order:

I. Generation of intracellular second messenger (cyclic AMP or Ca2+)

II. Induction of downstream intracellular biochemical responses

III. Binding of hormone to specific membrane-bound receptor on the plasma membrane

IV. Manifestation of final physiological responses (e.g., ovarian growth)

V. Formation of hormone-receptor complex on the cell surface producing Response 1

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Water-soluble peptide and protein hormones cannot diffuse through the lipid bilayer of the target cell plasma membrane; their signaling pathway operates via an extracellular receptor-activated secondary messenger cascade.

Step 2: Sequential Analysis of the Signal Transduction Cascade
- The initial molecular event is the recognition and physical binding of the circulating protein hormone (such as FSH) to its complementary membrane-bound receptor located on the target cell surface.
- This receptor engagement leads to the formation of a hormone-receptor complex that triggers conformational changes in the membrane, designated as Response 1.
- Response 1 subsequently activates membrane-associated enzymes (such as adenylate cyclase) to stimulate the generation of intracellular second messengers, notably cyclic AMP (cAMP) or ionic calcium (Ca2+).
- These second messengers diffuse through the cytosol to trigger downstream biochemical cascades and enzymatic phosphorylation reactions.
- Cumulative biochemical alterations culminate in observable cellular physiological responses, such as follicular development and ovarian growth.

Step 3: Logical Ordering and Verification
Arranging these steps chronologically yields the following order: binding of hormone to membrane-bound receptor, formation of hormone-receptor complex producing Response 1, generation of second messenger, initiation of biochemical responses, and manifestation of physiological responses.

Final Answer:
The correct chronological order begins with hormone binding to the membrane-bound receptor, followed by hormone-receptor complex formation, generation of second messengers, intracellular biochemical responses, and final physiological responses.

answer.text: III → V → I → II → IV
III → I → V → II → IV
V → III → I → IV → II
I → III → V → II → IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q02 - Sequence of molecular events in steroid hormone action

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following molecular events in the mechanism of action of a steroid hormone (e.g., estrogen) on its target uterine cell in the correct sequential order from initiation to physiological response:

I. Interaction of hormone-receptor complex with regulatory sequences on the genome (DNA)

II. Translation of transcribed mRNA into functional proteins

III. Diffusion of lipophilic steroid hormone across the target cell plasma membrane

IV. Synthesis of messenger RNA (mRNA) via genomic transcription

V. Binding of hormone to an intracellular nuclear receptor forming a hormone-receptor complex

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Steroid hormones are lipophilic molecules derived from cholesterol that cross cell membranes unhindered to regulate gene expression directly through intracellular nuclear receptors.

Step 2: Chronological Sequence of Intracellular Signaling
- Because of their hydrophobic lipid-soluble nature, steroid hormone molecules (such as estrogen) initially diffuse freely across the target cell plasma membrane.
- Inside the target cell, the hormone migrates into the nucleus and binds with high affinity to its specific intracellular nuclear receptor, forming an active hormone-receptor complex.
- The resulting hormone-receptor complex interacts physically with hormone response elements on the chromatin and nuclear genome (DNA).
- Interaction with the genome alters transcriptional regulation, initiating the synthesis of specific messenger RNA (mRNA) transcripts.
- The synthesized mRNA moves into the cytoplasm and undergoes translation on ribosomes to produce structural and enzymatic proteins, which mediate tissue growth and differentiation.

Step 3: Synthesis and Ordering Verification
Ordering these events from initiation to phenotypic outcome establishes the sequence: diffusion across the cell membrane, formation of the nuclear hormone-receptor complex, interaction with the genome, transcription into mRNA, and translation into functional proteins.

Final Answer:
The correct chronological sequence begins with diffusion across the plasma membrane, followed by intracellular receptor binding, genomic DNA interaction, mRNA transcription, and translation into functional proteins.

answer.text: III → I → V → IV → II
III → V → I → IV → II
V → III → I → II → IV
III → V → IV → I → II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q01 - Scientific definition of hormones as intercellular messengers

questiontext.text: According to the current scientific definition, hormones are accurately described as which of the following?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the classical versus scientific definition of hormones.
The classical definition described a hormone as a chemical produced by endocrine glands, released into blood, and transported to a distantly located target organ. However, the current scientific definition broadens this scope to cover additional signaling molecules.

Step 2: State the defining characteristics under the scientific definition.
Hormones are scientifically defined as non-nutrient chemicals that act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts.

Step 3: Evaluate physiological implications.
Because they act as intercellular messengers in minute quantities without providing caloric nutrition, substances acting as nutrient sources or required in bulk amounts do not fit this scientific definition.

Final Answer: Non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts.

answer.text: Non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts
Macronutrient chemicals transported via specialized ducts directly to target tissues
Nutrient molecules acting as intracellular energy sources produced in large quantities
Enzymatic secretions produced in abundant quantities that catalyze digestive hydrolyses

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q02 - Mechanism of hypothalamic regulation over pituitary gland

questiontext.text: How does the hypothalamus functionally and anatomically regulate the anterior and posterior lobes of the pituitary gland?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand hypothalamic neurosecretory connection to anterior pituitary.
Hypothalamic releasing and inhibiting hormones are produced by neurosecretory cells (nuclei), travel down axons, and are released at nerve endings into a portal circulatory system that transports them directly to the anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis).

Step 2: Understand hypothalamic connection to posterior pituitary.
The posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus. Hormones such as oxytocin and vasopressin are synthesised in hypothalamic neurons and transported axonally directly to the posterior pituitary for storage and release.

Step 3: Contrast both regulatory pathways.
The anterior pituitary is governed via the hypophyseal portal circulatory system, whereas the posterior pituitary is governed under direct neural axonal transport from the hypothalamus.

Final Answer: The anterior pituitary is regulated via a portal circulatory system, while the posterior pituitary is under direct neural regulation.

answer.text: Both anterior and posterior lobes are under direct neural regulation without any vascular transport mechanism
The anterior pituitary is regulated via a portal circulation, while the posterior pituitary is under direct neural regulation
Both anterior and posterior lobes are regulated exclusively via the hypophyseal portal circulation
The anterior pituitary is under direct neural control, while the posterior pituitary receives hormones via portal circulation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q03 - Inhibitory effect of somatostatin on growth hormone

questiontext.text: Which hypothalamic hormone is responsible for inhibiting the release of growth hormone from the pituitary gland?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the classes of hypothalamic hormones.
The hypothalamus produces two types of hormones: releasing hormones, which stimulate pituitary secretions, and inhibiting hormones, which suppress pituitary secretions.

Step 2: Analyze the specific action of somatostatin.
Somatostatin secreted by hypothalamic neurons acts directly on the anterior pituitary to inhibit the synthesis and release of growth hormone (GH). In contrast, Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulates gonadotrophin release.

Final Answer: Somatostatin from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.

Somatostatin

generalfeedback.text:

The pituitary gland is located at the base of the brain, attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk.

Step 2: Recall the specific cranial skeletal landmark.
The bony cavity of the sphenoid bone that houses and protects the pituitary gland is known as the sella tursica.

Final Answer: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q05 - Pathology and clinical presentation of adult acromegaly

questiontext.text: Hypersecretion of growth hormone in adults, particularly during middle age, leads to which clinical condition characterized by severe facial disfigurement?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand age-dependent effects of growth hormone oversecretion.
During childhood before epiphyseal plate closure, hypersecretion of growth hormone leads to abnormal elongation of long bones, termed gigantism.

Step 2: Analyze adult hypersecretion.
In adults, after the epiphyseal plates have fused, excess growth hormone cannot cause longitudinal bone growth. Instead, it leads to disproportionate thickening of bones and soft tissues, causing severe facial disfigurement and serious complications, a condition known as acromegaly.

Final Answer: Acromegaly results from excess secretion of growth hormone in adults, causing severe disfigurement especially of the face.

answer.text: Acromegaly

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q06 - Hormonal regulation of Leydig cells and spermatogenesis

questiontext.text: In human males, the specific target cells and physiological roles of luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) are:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the role and target of luteinizing hormone in males.
Luteinizing hormone (LH) acts on the interstitial cells (Leydig cells) located in the intertubular spaces of the testis to stimulate the synthesis and secretion of androgens, primarily testosterone.

Step 2: Identify the role of follicle stimulating hormone in males.
Follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) acts in conjunction with androgens to regulate and stimulate the process of spermatogenesis within the seminiferous tubules.

Final Answer: LH stimulates the secretion of androgens from Leydig cells, whereas FSH and androgens jointly regulate spermatogenesis.

questiontext.text: The pars intermedia region of the adenohypophysis secretes which hormone?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the anatomical subdivisions of adenohypophysis.
Adenohypophysis consists of pars distalis (anterior pituitary) and pars intermedia.

Step 2: Recall the hormone secreted by pars intermedia.
Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone, namely melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH). In humans, pars intermedia is almost entirely merged with pars distalis.

Final Answer: Pars intermedia secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q08 - Action of vasopressin and diabetes insipidus pathophysiology

questiontext.text: An impairment affecting the synthesis or release of anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) results in which condition, and what is its primary physiological cause?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review the physiological function of anti-diuretic hormone (vasopressin).
Vasopressin acts mainly on the distal convoluted tubules and collecting ducts of the nephron in the kidney, stimulating the resorption of water and electrolytes, thereby preventing excessive water loss through urine (diuresis).

Step 2: Evaluate the pathological consequence of ADH hyposecretion.
When synthesis or secretion of ADH is impaired, the kidney's ability to conserve water is diminished. This causes massive excretion of dilute urine and severe dehydration, a condition called Diabetes Insipidus.

Final Answer: Diabetes insipidus, caused by diminished ability of the kidney to conserve water due to ADH deficiency.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q09 - Physiological actions of oxytocin on female target organs

questiontext.text: Which of the following describes the physiological actions of oxytocin in the human female body?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify target tissues of oxytocin.
Oxytocin acts specifically on smooth muscle cells of the body.

Step 2: Analyze uterine action during parturition.
During child birth, oxytocin stimulates vigorous contractions of the uterine smooth muscles to facilitate delivery of the baby.

Step 3: Analyze action on mammary glands during lactation.
Oxytocin stimulates the contraction of myoepithelial cells surrounding mammary alveoli, causing milk ejection (let-down reflex). Prolactin, by contrast, stimulates milk synthesis and alveolar growth.

Final Answer: Stimulation of vigorous uterine contraction during childbirth and milk ejection from mammary glands.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q10 - Pineal gland location and physiological actions of melatonin

questiontext.text: Where is the pineal gland located, and what is the primary role of its secreted hormone, melatonin?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the anatomical location of pineal gland.
The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of the forebrain.

Step 2: Recall the primary hormonal role of melatonin.
Melatonin regulates the 24-hour diurnal rhythm of our body, including the sleep-wake cycle and body temperature, while also influencing metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle, and immune defense capability.

Final Answer: Located on the dorsal side of forebrain, regulating the 24-hour diurnal sleep-wake cycle and body temperature.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the essential role of thyroid hormones in fetal development.
Thyroid hormones are critical for central nervous system maturation, skeletal growth, and general tissue differentiation during embryonic development.

Step 2: Identify maternal iodine deficiency and hypothyroidism consequences.
Maternal hypothyroidism results in cretinism in the child, marked by stunted physical growth, mental retardation, low intelligence quotient (IQ), abnormal skin, and deaf-mutism.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q13 - Pathological features of exophthalmic goitre or Graves disease

questiontext.text: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism characterized by which combination of clinical features?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the underlying endocrine disorder.
Exophthalmic goitre is an autoimmune form of hyperthyroidism, caused by abnormal hypersecretion of thyroid hormones (\(T_3\) and \(T_4\)).

Step 2: Recognize the specific clinical diagnostic triad.
The condition is characterized by enlargement of the thyroid gland, prominent protrusion of the eyeballs (exophthalmos), heightened basal metabolic rate (BMR), and significant weight loss.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q14 - Regulation of blood calcium by PTH and TCT

questiontext.text: Blood calcium homeostasis in the human body is maintained by the coordinated antagonistic action of which two hormones?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the hypercalcemic hormone.
Parathyroid hormone (PTH), secreted by the parathyroid glands, increases blood \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) levels by promoting bone resorption, renal reabsorption of \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\), and dietary \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) absorption in the gut.

Step 2: Identify the hypocalcemic hormone.
Thyrocalcitonin (TCT), a protein hormone secreted by the thyroid gland, lowers circulating blood \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) levels.

Step 3: Analyze their antagonistic balance.
Together, PTH (hypercalcemic) and TCT (hypocalcemic) maintain blood calcium levels within precise physiological limits.

Final Answer: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) and Thyrocalcitonin (TCT).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q15 - Mechanisms by which parathyroid hormone elevates blood calcium

questiontext.text: Which of the following physiological processes is stimulated by parathyroid hormone (PTH) to elevate circulating \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) levels?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the target organs of PTH.
PTH acts on three main target sites: bone, renal tubules, and the gastrointestinal tract.

Step 2: Detail PTH actions on each target.
On bones, PTH stimulates bone resorption (demineralization/dissolution). In the kidney, it stimulates reabsorption of \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) by renal tubules. In the digestive tract, it increases \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) absorption from digested food.

Step 3: Conclude the collective physiological effect.
These actions collectively release calcium into the bloodstream, making PTH a hypercalcemic hormone.

Final Answer: Stimulation of bone resorption (demineralization), renal tubular reabsorption of calcium, and dietary calcium absorption.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q16 - Thymus anatomical location and age related degeneration

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify anatomical coordinates of thymus.
The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between the lungs, behind the sternum, on the ventral side of the aorta.

Step 2: Analyze age-dependent changes.
The thymus is large in infants and children but progressively degenerates in old individuals. This atrophy leads to a diminished production of thymosins, causing a corresponding decline in immune competence in elderly people.

Final Answer: Located between lungs behind sternum on the ventral side of aorta; degenerates with advancing age resulting in decreased thymosin production.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q19 - Etiology and clinical signs of Addison disease

questiontext.text: Underproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex leads to which pathological condition, and what is its physiological hallmark?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the endocrine organ and hormonal deficit.
Hyposecretion (underproduction) of corticoid hormones by the adrenal cortex.

Step 2: Relate hormonal deficiency to clinical presentation.
Underproduction of corticoids impairs carbohydrate metabolism and electrolyte balance, causing acute weakness and extreme fatigue, a syndrome termed Addison's disease.

Final Answer: Addison's disease, caused by underproduction of adrenal corticoids resulting in altered carbohydrate metabolism, acute weakness, and fatigue.

Cushing's syndrome, marked by excessive cortisol production and central adiposity
Addison's disease, marked by altered carbohydrate metabolism, acute weakness, and severe fatigue
Diabetes insipidus, marked by impaired ADH synthesis and profound polydipsia

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q20 - Sympathomimetic actions of adrenaline and noradrenaline

questiontext.text: Which set of physiological responses is triggered during emergency situations by the rapid release of catecholamines from the adrenal medulla?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify catecholamines and their stimuli.
Adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine) are secreted by the adrenal medulla during stress or emergency ('fight or flight').

Step 2: Enumerate physiological actions.
These hormones increase alertness, cause pupillary dilation, induce piloerection (raising of hairs), stimulate sweating, increase heart rate, enhance the strength of ventricular contraction, and elevate the respiratory rate. Metabolically, they stimulate glycogenolysis, lipolysis, and proteolysis.

Final Answer: Increased alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection, sweating, elevated heart rate, and glycogen breakdown.

answer.text: Somnolence, reduced cardiac output, peripheral vasodilation, and decreased blood glucose
Pupillary constriction, decreased heart rate, bronchoconstriction, and glycogen synthesis
Inhibition of lipolysis, reduction of sweating, decreased respiration, and hypoglycemia
Increased alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection, sweating, and increased heart rate

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q21 - Metabolic actions of cortisol on macromolecules and uptake

questiontext.text: Which of the following accurately describes the biochemical and metabolic actions mediated by cortisol (glucocorticoids)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze cortisol's impact on carbohydrate metabolism.
Cortisol promotes gluconeogenesis (synthesis of glucose from non-carbohydrate substrates like amino acids and glycerol), raising blood glucose.

Step 2: Analyze cortisol's impact on lipid and protein metabolism.
Cortisol stimulates lipolysis (breakdown of fats) and proteolysis (breakdown of proteins).

Step 3: Analyze cellular uptake of amino acids.
Cortisol inhibits cellular uptake and utilization of amino acids, ensuring they remain available in circulation as substrates for hepatic gluconeogenesis.

Final Answer: Stimulation of gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, and proteolysis, along with inhibition of cellular amino acid uptake and utilization.

answer.text: Stimulation of gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, and proteolysis, and inhibition of cellular amino acid uptake
Stimulation of glycogenesis, lipogenesis, and protein synthesis, and enhanced amino acid uptake
Inhibition of gluconeogenesis, stimulation of glycogen storage, and acceleration of proteolysis
Enhancement of cellular glucose uptake, stimulation of protein deposition, and inhibition of lipolysis

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q22 - Non metabolic physiological actions of cortisol

questiontext.text: In addition to carbohydrate metabolism, cortisol exerts which combination of systemic physiological actions in the human body?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examine cardiovascular and renal actions.
Cortisol is actively involved in maintaining cardiovascular system integrity and normal kidney functions.

Step 2: Examine immunological actions.
Cortisol produces potent anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response, making it clinically useful as an immunosuppressive agent.

Step 3: Examine hematological actions.
Cortisol stimulates the production of red blood cells (erythropoiesis).

Final Answer: Maintenance of cardiovascular and kidney functions, anti-inflammatory reactions, immunosuppression, and stimulation of RBC production.

answer.text: Depression of blood pressure, reduction of glomerular filtration rate, and destruction of erythrocytes
Maintenance of cardiovascular and renal functions, anti-inflammatory effects, immunosuppression, and stimulation of erythropoiesis
Enhancement of immune responsiveness, pro-inflammatory action, and inhibition of erythropoiesis
Stimulation of histamine release, enhancement of antibody production, and suppression of renal tubular function

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q23 - Transport actions of aldosterone in nephron

questiontext.text: What is the primary site of action and physiological role of aldosterone (mineralocorticoid)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify target site of aldosterone.
Aldosterone acts mainly on the renal tubules (specifically the distal parts of the nephron).

Step 2: Identify specific ionic and fluid shifts.
Aldosterone stimulates the reabsorption of \(\text{Na}^+\) and water, while concurrently stimulating the excretion of \(\text{K}^+\) and phosphate ions.

Step 3: Relate to systemic homeostasis.
Through these actions, aldosterone helps maintain body fluid volume, electrolytes, osmotic pressure, and blood pressure.

Final Answer: Acts at renal tubules to stimulate reabsorption of sodium and water, and excretion of potassium and phosphate ions.

answer.text: Acts on glomerulus to stimulate excretion of \(\text{Na}^+\) and water, while conserving \(\text{K}^+\)
Acts on hepatocytes to stimulate glycogen storage and decrease blood osmotic pressure
Acts on renal tubules to stimulate reabsorption of \(\text{Na}^+\) and water, and excretion of \(\text{K}^+\) and phosphate ions
Acts on collecting ducts to inhibit water reabsorption, producing copious hypotonic urine

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q24 - Endocrine proportion and cells of pancreas

questiontext.text: What proportion of total pancreatic tissue is constituted by the Islets of Langerhans, and what are their two primary endocrine cell types?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the numerical abundance of Islets of Langerhans.
In a normal human pancreas, there are about 1 to 2 million Islets of Langerhans, which represent only 1 to 2 percent of the total pancreatic tissue.

Step 2: Identify primary cell types and their secretions.
The two primary types of cells in the islets are \(\alpha\)-cells, which secrete glucagon, and \(\beta\)-cells, which secrete insulin.

Final Answer: 1 to 2 percent; comprising alpha-cells (glucagon) and beta-cells (insulin).

answer.text: 50 percent of pancreatic tissue; \(\alpha\)-cells secrete somatostatin and \(\beta\)-cells secrete gastrin
20 to 25 percent of pancreatic tissue; acinar cells secrete glucagon and ductal cells secrete insulin
10 to 15 percent of pancreatic tissue; \(\alpha\)-cells secrete insulin and \(\beta\)-cells secrete glucagon
1 to 2 percent of pancreatic tissue; \(\alpha\)-cells secrete glucagon and \(\beta\)-cells secrete insulin

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q25 - Antagonistic actions of insulin and glucagon

questiontext.text: How do insulin and glucagon antagonistically regulate blood glucose levels in humans?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze glucagon's mechanism.
Glucagon acts primarily on hepatocytes, stimulating glycogenolysis (breakdown of glycogen into glucose) and gluconeogenesis, while reducing cellular glucose uptake and utilization. This elevates blood sugar, making glucagon a hyperglycemic hormone.

Step 2: Analyze insulin's mechanism.
Insulin acts on hepatocytes and adipocytes to enhance cellular glucose uptake and utilization, and stimulates glycogenesis (conversion of glucose to glycogen). This moves glucose from blood into cells, making insulin a hypoglycemic hormone.

Step 3: Synthesize glucose homeostasis.
Blood glucose concentration is maintained dynamically between meals by the balance of these opposing actions.

Final Answer: Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis (hyperglycemic), while insulin enhances cellular uptake and glycogenesis (hypoglycemic).

answer.text: Glucagon promotes glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis to elevate blood glucose, while insulin stimulates cellular glucose uptake and glycogenesis to lower blood glucose
Glucagon lowers blood sugar by accelerating glycolysis, while insulin elevates blood sugar via glycogenolysis
Glucagon stimulates glycogenesis in muscle, while insulin promotes gluconeogenesis in hepatocytes
Both hormones enhance cellular glucose uptake by adipocytes, but only glucagon stimulates renal reabsorption

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q26 - Hormonal control over glycogenolysis gluconeogenesis and glycogenesis pathways

questiontext.text: Which metabolic pathways are stimulated by glucagon and insulin, respectively, in hepatocytes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Detail glucagon-mediated hepatic pathways.
Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis (cleavage of stored glycogen into glucose) and gluconeogenesis (de novo synthesis of glucose from non-hexose precursors).

Step 2: Detail insulin-mediated hepatic pathways.
Insulin stimulates glycogenesis (polymerization of glucose into glycogen) and inhibits glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.

Step 3: Compare both hormones.
Thus, glucagon drives pathways that release free glucose into circulation, whereas insulin drives pathways that sequester glucose as storage polymers.

Final Answer: Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, whereas insulin stimulates glycogenesis.

answer.text: Glucagon stimulates proteolysis and glycogenesis; insulin stimulates gluconeogenesis and lipolysis
Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis; insulin stimulates glycogenesis
Glucagon stimulates glycolysis and glycogenesis; insulin stimulates gluconeogenesis
Glucagon stimulates glycogenesis and lipogenesis; insulin stimulates glycogenolysis

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q27 - Clinical markers and pathological features of diabetes mellitus

questiontext.text: Prolonged hyperglycemia associated with diabetes mellitus leads to which pair of characteristic clinical features?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the physiological deficit in diabetes mellitus.
Diabetes mellitus is caused by a deficiency of insulin and/or insulin resistance, leading to persistent, severe hyperglycemia.

Step 2: Identify characteristic urinary and metabolic findings.
When blood glucose exceeds renal threshold, glucose is lost through urine (glycosuria). In addition, incomplete breakdown of fats leads to the formation and excretion of toxic ketone bodies (ketonuria/ketosis).

Final Answer: Loss of glucose through urine and formation of harmful compounds known as ketone bodies.

answer.text: Excessive retention of water in body tissues and absence of urinary solutes
Excretion of large quantities of dilute urine devoid of glucose or ketone bodies
Loss of glucose through urine (glycosuria) and formation of harmful ketone bodies
Deposition of excess glycogen in renal tubules and hypercalcemia

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q28 - Endocrine role of Leydig cells in the testis

questiontext.text: Which cells present in the intertubular spaces of the human testis produce the steroid hormones known as androgens?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify testicular histology.
The testis is composed of seminiferous tubules embedded within stromal or interstitial tissue.

Step 2: Identify androgen-producing cells.
The interstitial cells or Leydig cells, located in the intertubular spaces between seminiferous tubules, synthesize and secrete androgens, primarily testosterone.

Final Answer: Leydig cells (interstitial cells) produce androgens.

answer.text: Spermatogonia
Follicular cells
Sertoli cells
Leydig cells (interstitial cells)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q29 - Physiological and metabolic actions of testicular androgens

questiontext.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the physiological and metabolic effects mediated by androgens in human males?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify reproductive and secondary sexual actions.
Androgens regulate the development, maturation, and functions of male accessory sex organs (epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles, prostate, urethra), stimulate spermatogenesis, and promote male secondary sexual traits (muscular growth, facial/axillary hair, low voice pitch).

Step 2: Identify behavioral and metabolic effects.
Androgens act on the central neural system to influence male libido, and produce anabolic (synthetic) effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism.

Final Answer: Stimulation of male accessory organs, secondary sex characters, spermatogenesis, libido, and anabolic effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism.

answer.text: Stimulation of accessory sex organs, secondary sexual traits, spermatogenesis, libido, and anabolic metabolic effects
Exclusive regulation of renal sodium excretion without any effects on somatic or reproductive tissues
Stimulation of high pitch voice, catabolic breakdown of skeletal muscle, and inhibition of spermatogenesis
Inhibition of libido, atrophy of seminal vesicles, and stimulation of mammary duct branching

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q30 - Endocrine transformation of ruptured Graafian follicle

questiontext.text: Following ovulation, the ruptured Graafian follicle transforms into a temporary endocrine structure called the:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Trace the fate of ovarian follicles post-ovulation.
After the release of an ovum during ovulation, the remnants of the ruptured Graafian follicle undergo luteinization.

Step 2: Identify the resulting structure and hormone.
The transformed structure is called the corpus luteum, which acts as an endocrine body that secretes mainly progesterone.

Final Answer: Corpus luteum, which primarily secretes progesterone.

answer.text: Corpus callosum
Corpus luteum
Macula lutea
Corpus albicans

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q31 - Differentiating physiological actions of estrogen and progesterone

questiontext.text: How do the primary physiological roles of estrogen and progesterone differ in the female body?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the roles of estrogen.
Estrogen, secreted mainly by growing ovarian follicles, stimulates the development of female secondary sex organs, appearance of secondary sex characters (e.g., high pitch voice), development of ovarian follicles, and regulates female sexual behavior.

Step 2: Identify the roles of progesterone.
Progesterone, secreted by the corpus luteum, supports and maintains pregnancy, and acts on mammary glands to stimulate the formation of alveoli (sac-like structures that store milk) and milk secretion.

Step 3: Contrast their distinct targets and timing.
Estrogen drives follicular growth and secondary sexual differentiation, whereas progesterone prepares and maintains the uterine/gestational environment and alveolar structures.

Final Answer: Estrogen stimulates female secondary sex organs and secondary sex characteristics, while progesterone supports pregnancy and stimulates mammary alveolar development.

answer.text: Estrogen is secreted exclusively during pregnancy, while progesterone is secreted only during the early follicular phase
Estrogen inhibits development of secondary sex organs, while progesterone stimulates male-pattern muscular growth
Estrogen promotes female secondary sex characteristics and follicular development, while progesterone supports pregnancy and stimulates alveolar development in mammary glands
Estrogen maintains the corpus luteum during gestation, while progesterone induces ovulation of mature Graafian follicles

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q32 - Vasodilatory action of atrial natriuretic factor

questiontext.text: When blood pressure rises, which peptide hormone is secreted by the heart, and how does it lower blood pressure?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify cardiac endocrine secretion.
The atrial wall of the heart secretes a peptide hormone called atrial natriuretic factor (ANF).

Step 2: Mechanism of action of ANF.
ANF is secreted in response to increased blood pressure or atrial stretch. It causes dilation of blood vessels (vasodilation), which decreases peripheral vascular resistance, thereby reducing blood pressure.

Final Answer: Atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), which causes dilation of blood vessels to decrease blood pressure.

answer.text: Renin, which causes systemic vasoconstriction to reduce blood pressure
Aldosterone, which increases water excretion by renal tubules to lower blood pressure
Angiotensin, which dilates renal arterioles to decrease central venous pressure
Atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), which causes vasodilation to reduce blood pressure

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q33 - Secretion site and physiological role of erythropoietin

questiontext.text: Erythropoietin, a peptide hormone that stimulates erythropoiesis (RBC formation), is produced by which specialized cells?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the organ and specific cell population producing erythropoietin.
In the human kidney, specialized cells of the juxtaglomerular apparatus known as juxtaglomerular (JG) cells produce erythropoietin.

Step 2: Recall its physiological function.
Erythropoietin acts on bone marrow erythroid progenitor cells to stimulate erythropoiesis (the formation of red blood cells).

Final Answer: Juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney.

answer.text: Juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney
Chromaffin cells of adrenal medulla
Podocytes of Bowman's capsule
Acinar cells of the pancreas

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q34 - Target organs and secretory responses of gastrointestinal hormones

questiontext.text: Which of the following correctly pairs a gastrointestinal peptide hormone with its specific target tissue and physiological action?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review gastrin.
Gastrin acts on gastric glands and stimulates secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) and pepsinogen.

Step 2: Review secretin.
Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas to stimulate secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.

Step 3: Review CCK and GIP.
Cholecystokinin (CCK) acts on both the pancreas and gall bladder, stimulating secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice, respectively. Gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP) inhibits gastric secretion and motility.

Step 4: Select the verified pairing.
Secretin acting on exocrine pancreas to stimulate secretion of water and bicarbonate ions matches the precise NCERT physiological assignment.

Final Answer: Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas to stimulate the secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.

answer.text: Gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP) stimulates gastric acid secretion and accelerates stomach motility
Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions
Cholecystokinin (CCK) acts on gastric glands to stimulate secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen
Gastrin acts on the gall bladder and stimulates contraction to release bile juice

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_MCQ_Q35 - Dual action of CCK on gallbladder and pancreas

questiontext.text: Cholecystokinin (CCK) acts on two distinct digestive organs to stimulate which secretions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify target organs of CCK.
CCK acts simultaneously on the gall bladder and the exocrine pancreas.

Step 2: Detail the respective secretory responses.
It stimulates the gall bladder to contract and release bile juice, and it stimulates the exocrine pancreas to secrete pancreatic digestive enzymes.

Final Answer: Stimulates secretion of bile juice from gall bladder and pancreatic enzymes from pancreas.

answer.text: Secretion of water and bicarbonate ions from pancreas and mucus from intestinal crypts
